transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Rita Gomez (Redwood CSM), Alex Carter (CTO, Orchestrion Labs), Priya Singh (Eng Manager), Jonas Meyer (SRE), Elena Ruiz (Product), Samir Patel (Data Scientist)

Summary:
Quick QBR focusing on recent burst in latency (what Orchestrion called 'latency burn'), cost variance from forecast, and roadmap alignment for next quarter. Agreed to run a focused latency regression with dedicated capacity options and share SOC2/security artifacts. Decided on concrete next steps and owners.

Topics Covered:
- Recent latency spike and root-cause hypotheses (batching, KV cache misses, tokenization change)
- Cost overrun drivers (hot routes, non-expiring caches, quantization settings)
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for predictable latency
- Roadmap items: prioritized guardrails, regression alerts, and an eval set for Orchestrion's top flows
- Security/compliance ask: KMS, audit log retention, SSO mapping

Action items (captured in metadata):
1) Maya to share security pack and SOC2 snapshot
2) Daniel to run latency bench (2h) with Jonas
3) Priya to send top prompts and latency SLOs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time, happy valentine's day if you're celebrating, we'll be concise. quick roll call?
[00:11] Alex (Orchestrion CTO): Alex here.
[00:13] Priya (Eng Mgr): priya.
[00:15] Jonas (SRE): Jonas.
[00:18] Daniel (Redwood SE): daniel on my side, thanks.
[00:20] Rita (CSM): rita here.
[00:22] Samir (Data Sci): samir.
[00:24] Elena (Product): elena joining.

[00:30] Maya: quick agenda: 1) understand the latency burn you saw last week, 2) cost delta, 3) route to mitigate this quarter, and 4) next steps on security and roadmap. is that right priya?
[00:39] Priya: yea that's right.

[02:05] Alex: so to summarize, on tuesday we had a spike — p95 jumped from 210ms to around 1.2s for our critical text completion route. It triggered our alarms, impacted 6% of requests, user complaints went up. We reverted a tokenizer tweak but the numbers didn't go fully back down.

[03:00] Jonas: i looked at pod metrics — there were unusually high KV cache misses and concurrent small requests that didn't batch well. we also had a short autoscale lag.

[03:40] Daniel: okay, KV — sometimes it's the prefix cache warming, if a tokenizer change introduced different token sequences it can bust your prefixes. also our continuous batching settings can cause smaller tails to run without joining batches if the inter-arrival times change.

[04:25] Samir: we shipped a small prompt template change which increased average sequence length slightly; maybe that had a multiplier effect.

[05:00] Elena: on the cost side, our bill jumped 18% month-over-month. we were expecting 6%.

[05:17] Maya: that's a sizable delta. is that across all models or concentrated on the completion route?
[05:24] Priya: mostly completion and a rerank endpoint we use for search.

[06:00] Daniel: rerank tends to be heavy because of repeated short calls — if those aren't cached properly or if you're hitting a non-quantized variant it adds up. Are you on the quantized flavor for the smaller model?

[06:31] Priya: we thought we were on q4 quantized but we've got a mix. ops changed a config for canary and it inadvertently routed some traffic to the full-precision instance.

[07:05] Jonas: and add that we had a long-lived pin for a version on Redwood Dedicate — i mean Redwood Dedicated — that didn't autoscale as expected because of the policy.

[07:28] Maya: ok, so three buckets: cache/prefix, batching config, and variant routing/quantization mismatch. Do we have logs showing which user flows hit which variants?

[07:45] Priya: yeah but it's messy. our current tracing tags don't map cleanly to the model routing in your console.

[08:30] Rita: we can help map token-level attribution. i'll put a template in the shared drive after this call.

[09:02] Alex: curious about dedicated capacity options. If we moved to a small Reserved pool for the heavy routes, would that smooth the p95?

[09:20] Daniel: yes, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and less noisy neighbors, but there's a cost commitment. there's also an intermediate: reserve a minimal burst pool or a hybrid route where critical traffic is pinned to dedicated and the rest stays hosted.

[10:05] Alex: what's the expected cost delta? like order of magnitude?

[10:12] Maya: depends on QPS and token throughput. we'll model it — i can share a quick back-of-envelope during the week.

[11:00] Samir: another ask: we need regression alerts tied to our eval prompts. last incident we only noticed after user reports.

[11:20] Daniel: we've got a feature in Redwood Optimize that can run evals and trigger alerts on quality or latency regressions for a set. Have you got an eval corpus?

[11:40] Priya: we have a 200-prompt set but only 50 are production-critical. we'll share the 50.

[12:05] Daniel: perfect — we can wire that into a smoke test and set a 95th percentile latency guardrail.

[12:40] Jonas: on the infra side, we want clearer autoscale hooks. last time the scale-up lag cost us a minute of degraded perf. is there recommended config?

[13:12] Daniel: yes, set the route-level min replicas plus a conservative warmup — also continuous batching window tweaks. i'll send a runbook after we run the bench.

[14:00] Elena: security question — audit log retention, KMS integration and SSO. Can Redwood fit our compliance window?

[14:16] Maya: short answer: yes. we support KMS/HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated; hosted customers can use customer-managed KMS via bring-your-own keys in certain regions. We have SOC2 Type II and an ISO-thing but let me send the specific artifacts.

[14:50] Alex: any constraints around on-prem or VPC? we might need a private control plane for some ingested telemetry.

[15:02] Daniel: we have Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — on-prem is heavier lift, VPC-hosted private control plane can be quicker. we'll align with your security team.

[15:35] Priya: timeline question: if we want canary dedicated for a single route by end of Q1, is that realistic?

[15:45] Maya: yes, realistic. need to scope the QPS and token throughput, and sign a short reserve if you want predictability.

[17:00] Alex: ok, how about running a 2-hour bench where we replay a day's worth of critical traffic at 3x for 30 minutes and watch the p95?

[17:20] Daniel: we can do that with Jonas, use your top-50 prompts, and we'll test both hosted and a temporary dedicated pool. we'll capture token-level breakdowns.

[18:05] Jonas: for bench we need a runbook, data scrubbed of PII, and an agreed window. we can do early next week.

[18:35] Samir: small note — our tokenization change was to add emojis to prompts, that changed sequence distribution. maybe silly but it matters.

[19:05] Maya: ha, emojis are sneaky performance hits. good to know.

[20:00] Elena: product-wise we want to prioritize the rerank route optimization this quarter — it's the main cost driver.

[20:20] Daniel: for rerank we recommend model consolidation + caching top candidates plus small quantized reranker. that usually chops cost by 30-40% if accuracy tolerates it.

[21:15] Priya: what about transient spikes — fallback strategies?

[21:30] Maya: you can set a fallback policy to a cheaper variant or to a cached answer; Redwood supports automatic fallback by policy. we can show config examples.

[22:00] Alex: any mention of competitors? we did a POC with InferStream last quarter; their latency was ok but the routing and ops were more manual.

[22:25] Maya: yeah, that matches other customers' feedback — InferStream needs heavier ops glue. CloudEndpoint's pricing looked cheaper in some runs but reliability was variable.

[23:00] Rita: circling back to security, i'll drop the SOC2 and an extraction of audit log retention limits into the shared folder today.

[23:20] Priya: great.

[24:00] Maya: recap of next steps: Maya send security docs and a high-level dedicated cost model; Daniel schedule bench with Jonas for next week; Priya share top 50 prompts and SLOs; Rita share mapping template. anyone object?

[24:25] Alex: no objections.

[25:00] Elena: can we also have a short extra 30-min follow-up after the bench to review results?

[25:12] Daniel: yes we'll schedule that.

[26:00] Priya: timeline — bench by 2/21, results review 2/22, decision on dedicated reserve 2/28?

[26:20] Maya: that timeline seems feasible.

[27:00] Samir: one last operational ask — expose token-level cost per route in the console for our billing team.

[27:18] Maya: that's on the roadmap and we can provide an interim csv export.

[28:00] Jonas: small nit — in your console the model variant name was hyphenated differently than what we label in infra, confusion there. can we align names to avoid accidental routing?

[28:20] Daniel: yes we'll reconcile naming; i'll coordinate with your infra team.

[29:00] Alex: thanks everyone — very helpful.
[29:10] Maya: thanks all, rita will share artifacts. we'll follow up with the bench invite.
[29:25] End of recording.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearing of product names (Redwood Dedicated transcribed once as Redwood Dedicate), KV cache spelled out as K V cash in some logs, minor punctuation/pauses missing.
